correctness.rationale: For the exact stated signature, information-order monotonicity forbids Boolean-incomplete columns and compatible pairs. Explicit coordinate selector terms e_i and h_i generate each prescribed coordinate pattern, proving iff. Cube volume and a matching construction prove the sharp rank and matching bijection. In the random model, all nine two-letter cases yield 7 compatibles, all 27 three-letter cases yield 17 simultaneous compatibles; dependency-graph Poisson error is O(m^3(7/9)^{2k}+m^3(17/27)^k), which vanishes on the claimed scale. Nongeneration due to no undefined symbol has probability at most m(2/3)^k ->0. A direct Python closure checker independently exhausts all tuples with m,k<=3; perfect matchings checked through k=4. The code is not substituted for asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: The full-generation problem is natural for finite powers representing partial Boolean functions in the new subreflexive-logic semantics. A necessary-and-sufficient tuple criterion, exact minimal rank, extremal perfect-matching interpretation and a quantitative random-generation transition answer related structural and probabilistic questions. The limiting nontrivial success law separates exceptional optimal generators from typical random tuples at a much larger scale. This is more than a renaming of the already known random-subcube edge threshold: the algebraic bridge and Poisson-width law provide distinct actionable information.
